Perhaps the perfect casual online game. At least for me. And when I say that, I don't mean that the game is at all perfect in its construction--it most certainly is not. All I mean is that the game is incredibly entertaining to casually play. A daily log on for an hour or so lets you complete some events, experiment with your build, do some challenges, and explore Appalachia (which is a pretty stellar example of map design) a bit more. It kills time in a very Bethesda way and genuinely has some pretty great moments and gameplay loops.

Recommended! This is not the Citizen Kane or Jeanne Deilman of games, but it doesn't need to be in order to be fun. Yes, Fallout 1st is annoying and it has a number of features that should be in the base game locked behind it (not a subscriber, btw). But honestly, if Fallout 1st, which actually has some pretty good, fair benefits, is your most despicable example of corporate greed--you should probably get out more.

(Also, I didn't get this for free. I pre-ordered this back in the Bethesda.net launcher days.)

The Fallout games are some of the best games ever made but 76 is completely marred at every corner.
This is a brutal inventory management simulator. It is easy to get resources but there is so many different kinds that you need for all kinds of different reasons that all weigh too much. Even if everything was 1/3rd of it's current weight it'd still be too much. Bethesda created an obvious solution to one of the top 3 most valuable resources the junk scrap needed to make and repair everything by making the Scrap Box. Something we all should have but they put up a paywall for it. Not just a pay wall but a ridiculous priced one at that. Especially after playing with a free trial of Fallout 1st I feel like I can't play without it. Private Servers is understandable to need more money for a botched title especially at launch but we want to play offline anyways. Access to explore & discover in peace especially to loot a place that isn't combed through by another player possibly missing out on something valuable that you needed that may never know was ever there to come back to. It's obvious to everyone that 76 was a failure that sum fans like myself want to come back to. The brutal inventory management that will eat all of your free time is just too much to allow you to do enjoy a damn game.

Fallout 76 feels like paying full price for a glorified cash shop with a game awkwardly bolted onto it. The gameplay is painfully clunky, the combat has all the depth of swatting flies, the graphics are mediocre at best, and the whole experience is mind-numbingly boring. Grinding through a world where nearly every enemy dies in a single hit isn't satisfying, it's just a complete waste of time.

And no, "it gets good in the endgame" is not a valid argument. If a game has to waste dozens of hours before it supposedly becomes enjoyable, then it has already failed at the one thing games are supposed to do: be fun. Fallout 76 is absurdly easy, has one of the worst user interfaces I've seen in a modern game, feels cheap in almost every aspect, and constantly reminds you that its real priority is selling you things through its cash shop.

I genuinely cannot understand why anyone would willingly spend both money and hundreds of hours on this pile of garbage.
